text: opus5-26 starting: computer-window node (VNC/RDP/local switch) + terminal-over-PTY. Reading the VNC implementation and researching what RDP-in-a-browser actually costs before writing any code.

Computer window node proved in a real browser. 8 cases green against a patched runtime, red without it (no protocol switch exists). vnc-node.test.mjs 7/7 still green against the same patched runtime. RDP verdict: it needs a gateway (guacd + a websocket tunnel), there is no JavaScript RDP client anywhere, and guacd has no native Windows build. Writing that up now.

Done. patch.json has 11 braindump.js hunks + 2 braindump.css hunks, all 13 anchors re-verified unique against the live file. Computer window node: VNC works exactly as before, RDP/Terminal/Local each say what they need with the real command and open no socket at all. RDP answer: no JavaScript RDP client exists anywhere, every browser-RDP product runs a gateway, and guacd has no native Windows build so on this machine it is Docker or WSL. RDP is safer on the wire (TLS + NLA vs VNC's 8-char DES) but adding a gateway is a net increase in surface here, and the UX argument is the stronger half. Terminal needs a PTY host and I did not add one: the preview server binds broadly and does not check Origin, and a WebSocket is not covered by CORS, so that would be a shell for every site you visit. Notes in .tmp/scratch/opus5-26/notes.md.
